v.title: Pérez Rips at Tebas, Barcelona Fans Brace for LaLiga Fallout
v.excerpt: Pérez slams Tebas, sparking a new LaLiga power struggle that could reshape Barcelona’s future in the league.
v.body:
## Quick take
Florentino Pérez has called Javier Tebas’ refusal to resign “outrageous,” igniting a fresh feud that could ripple through LaLiga and the Catalan capital’s footballing politics.

## What happened
Pérez, the Real Madrid president, took to a press conference to denounce the LaLiga chief’s decision to stay on after the club’s controversial move to the newly built Santiago Bernabéu.  He accused Tebas of “sabotaging” the sport and said the league’s image was at stake.  The comments came as the league is preparing to launch its new “Negreira” reform package, which Madrid has long opposed.

In response, Tebas issued a terse statement saying Pérez’s remarks were “unnecessary” and that the league’s governance structure would remain intact.  He hinted that any attempt to force a resignation would be met with legal and administrative push‑back, effectively stalling any real change.

## Why it matters
- **Barcelona’s position in LaLiga** – With the league’s reforms under scrutiny, Barça could benefit from a weakened Madrid‑Tebas alliance.  A more balanced governing body might open the door for fairer disciplinary measures and scheduling that protect our players’ fitness.
- **Impact on the 2026‑27 season** – The dispute could delay the rollout of the new league calendar, affecting transfer windows and fixture congestion.  Barcelona’s squad depth will be tested if the season starts later or features more midweek games.
- **Long‑term club politics** – A public split between the league’s top executives signals a power struggle that could influence future contracts, broadcasting deals, and the distribution of revenue.  Barça’s board must stay alert to any shifts that could alter the competitive balance.

## What's next
Watch the next LaLiga board meeting, scheduled for early next month, where the board will vote on Tebas’ future.  If he remains, we could see a new committee formed to address Madrid’s grievances, potentially reshaping the league’s executive structure.  For Barcelona, the outcome will dictate whether we can push for reforms that protect our players and maintain a level playing field.  Stay tuned for the official decision and any ripple effects on the upcoming season’s calendar.

*Source: [Madrid chief Pérez: "outrageous" that LaLiga president Tebas hasn't resigned](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50549300/florentino-perez-javier-tebas-laliga-negreira-real-madrid)*
